purpose: Reproducible inventory of the Zenodo dispatch source before creation of the teaching package.

source.title: U.S. Test System with High Spatial and Temporal Resolution for Renewable Integration Studies

texas_teaching_candidate.interpretation: The requested approximately 2,000-bus Texas system is present in the selected Zenodo archive. It is a Texas interconnect slice of the larger synthetic U.S. system, not an official ERCOT network model and not the separate ACTIVSg2000 artifact.

actions: Expand the eight retained Texas zonal demand profiles to bus demand using source Pd shares.
Normalize dispatch units and operating-limit fields.
Validate DC boundary treatment and generator profile coverage in the dispatch model.
Create validation reports and hashes before selecting student-visible candidate sites.

extraction_run.profile_decision: demand.csv is zonal demand for zone IDs 301-308 and should be disaggregated to Texas buses using the source bus Pd shares. Renewable profiles are plant-ID keyed and the Texas plant columns are retained in the extracted artifact.

benchmark_dispatch.formulation: linear DC balance with generator bounds, branch thermal limits, linear marginal costs, and optional load shedding
benchmark_dispatch.scope: small benchmark validation only; not a 2,000-bus production solver

production_dcopf.formulation: single-period linear DCOPF with generator bounds, MW-scaled branch thermal limits, optional load shedding, and linear marginal costs
production_dcopf.dc_boundary_convention: fixed injections at Texas receiving buses from source Pt values: 190 MW and 550 MW
production_dcopf.multi_period_use: call once per period; apply renewable availability and student load/storage decisions in the evaluator layer

caveats: The counts above are archive inventory counts, not yet the final student-visible teaching model.
The plant table contains generator records; dispatch variables and operating constraints still require a separate evaluator contract.

The first DCOPF path uses fixed base-case DC-tie injections; bidirectional tie scheduling, storage dynamics, renewable availability, and candidate data-center load remain evaluator-layer integrations.
